---
title: "Judges"
---

# Judges

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Judges describes Israel's repeated cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance. The book demonstrates humanity's need for a righteous King who can faithfully lead God's people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Judges 1:2</div>

<div class="identifier">Judah shall go up</div>

### Why This Verse

Beginning of conquest after Joshua

### Chapter Insight

This chapter describes Israel's incomplete conquest of Canaan. The key verse highlights the consequences of failing to fully obey God's commands.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Judges 2:10</div>

<div class="identifier">Another generation knew not the LORD</div>

### Why This Verse

Key theme of Judges

### Chapter Insight

This chapter explains Israel's recurring cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance. The key verse summarizes the spiritual decline that defines the book.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Judges 3:9</div>

<div class="identifier">The LORD raised up a deliverer</div>

### Why This Verse

Introduces the judge cycle

### Chapter Insight

This chapter introduces the first judges raised up by God. The key verse emphasizes God's mercy in providing deliverers for His people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 4

<div class="key-verse">Judges 4:9</div>

<div class="identifier">The honor shall not be yours</div>

### Why This Verse

Deborah's prophecy to Barak

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Deborah and Barak's victory over Sisera. The key verse highlights God's power working through faithful leaders.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 5

<div class="key-verse">Judges 5:31</div>

<div class="identifier">Let them that love Him be as the sun</div>

### Why This Verse

Conclusion of Deborah's song

### Chapter Insight

This chapter celebrates victory through the Song of Deborah. The key verse praises God for delivering Israel through willing servants.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 6

<div class="key-verse">Judges 6:12</div>

<div class="identifier">The LORD is with thee, mighty man of valor</div>

### Why This Verse

Gideon's famous call

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recounts Gideon's call to deliver Israel. The key verse emphasizes God's presence rather than human strength.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 7

<div class="key-verse">Judges 7:2</div>

<div class="identifier">Lest Israel boast</div>

### Why This Verse

God's purpose in reducing the army

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Gideon's victory with a reduced army. The key verse demonstrates that salvation belongs to the Lord alone.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 8

<div class="key-verse">Judges 8:23</div>

<div class="identifier">The LORD shall rule over you</div>

### Why This Verse

Gideon's refusal of kingship

### Chapter Insight

This chapter concludes Gideon's leadership and reveals Israel's continuing spiritual weakness. The key verse warns against forgetting God's deliverance.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 9

<div class="key-verse">Judges 9:8</div>

<div class="identifier">The trees went forth to anoint a king</div>

### Why This Verse

Jotham's famous parable

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Abimelech's violent pursuit of power. The key verse illustrates the destructive consequences of selfish ambition.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 10

<div class="key-verse">Judges 10:16</div>

<div class="identifier">His soul was grieved for Israel</div>

### Why This Verse

God's compassion despite rebellion

### Chapter Insight

This chapter describes Israel's renewed rebellion and suffering. The key verse reveals God's grief over His people's persistent unfaithfulness.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 11

<div class="key-verse">Judges 11:30</div>

<div class="identifier">Jephthah made a vow</div>

### Why This Verse

Beginning of the tragic vow account

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recounts Jephthah's rise and tragic vow. The key verse emphasizes faith in God's deliverance while warning against rash commitments.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 12

<div class="key-verse">Judges 12:6</div>

<div class="identifier">Shibboleth</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous origin of the term

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records conflict among the tribes and the ministry of additional judges. The key verse highlights the divisions resulting from pride and rivalry.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 13

<div class="key-verse">Judges 13:5</div>

<div class="identifier">He shall begin to deliver Israel</div>

### Why This Verse

Samson's birth announcement

### Chapter Insight

This chapter announces the birth of Samson. The key verse reveals God's sovereign preparation of a deliverer.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 14

<div class="key-verse">Judges 14:14</div>

<div class="identifier">Out of the eater came forth meat</div>

### Why This Verse

Samson's riddle

### Chapter Insight

This chapter begins Samson's public ministry. The key verse demonstrates God's ability to accomplish His purposes through imperfect people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 15

<div class="key-verse">Judges 15:16</div>

<div class="identifier">With the jawbone of a donkey</div>

### Why This Verse

Samson's victory song

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Samson's conflicts with the Philistines. The key verse highlights God's empowering strength in battle.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 16

<div class="key-verse">Judges 16:28</div>

<div class="identifier">O Lord GOD, remember me</div>

### Why This Verse

Samson's final prayer

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recounts Samson's downfall and final victory. The key verse demonstrates that God's grace can still work through repentance.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 17

<div class="key-verse">Judges 17:6</div>

<div class="identifier">Every man did what was right in his own eyes</div>

### Why This Verse

One of Judges' defining verses

### Chapter Insight

This chapter introduces Micah's idolatry. The key verse reveals the spiritual confusion caused by abandoning God's standards.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 18

<div class="key-verse">Judges 18:1</div>

<div class="identifier">In those days there was no king in Israel</div>

### Why This Verse

Sets context for tribal disorder

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records the tribe of Dan's migration and idolatry. The key verse illustrates the consequences of self-directed religion.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 19

<div class="key-verse">Judges 19:30</div>

<div class="identifier">Consider it, take counsel, and speak</div>

### Why This Verse

Response to national outrage

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recounts one of Israel's darkest moral failures. The key verse demonstrates the depth of national spiritual decay.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 20

<div class="key-verse">Judges 20:18</div>

<div class="identifier">They inquired of God</div>

### Why This Verse

Beginning of civil war account

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records civil war against Benjamin. The key verse highlights the devastating consequences of unchecked sin.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 21

<div class="key-verse">Judges 21:25</div>

<div class="identifier">Every man did what was right in his own eyes</div>

### Why This Verse

Closing summary of the book

### Chapter Insight

This chapter concludes with efforts to preserve Benjamin. The key verse summarizes the book's theme of moral chaos without godly leadership.
:::
